questions.question: Find the principal amount if the interest compounded annually at the rate of 10% for two years is ₹ 4,200.
questions.questionHtml: Find the principal amount if the interest compounded annually at the rate of 10% for two years is ₹ 4,200.
questions.solution:
Given:

The interest compounded annually at the rate of 10% for two years is ₹ 4,200.
Formula used:

Compound interest for 'n' years = \(P\left( 1+ \frac{r}{100}\right)^n-P\), where P is the principal amount and r is the interest rate per annum.
Calculation:
Compound interest for two years = 4200 = \(P\left( 1+ \frac{10}{100}\right)^2-P\)

Solving for P,

\(4200=P(1.21)-P\)

\(P=\frac{4200}{0.21}=20000\)

∴ The principal amount for the given case is Rs. 20,000

Shortcut Trick Ratio method - Interest = 10% = 1/10

1st year            2nd year

10                  11

 10                  11

100                  121   

P = 100 , A = 121, I = 121 -100 = 21

21→ 4200, 1→ 20, P = 20 × 100 = 20,000

questions.question: On a certain sum, the difference between compound interest and simple interest at 10% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 250. The sum is ______.
questions.questionHtml: On a certain sum, the difference between compound interest and simple interest at 10% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 250. The sum is ______.
questions.solution:
Given:

The difference between compound interest and simple interest at 10% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 250.

Formula used:

SI = \(\frac{(P × R × T)}{100}\)

CI = P(1 + R%)T - P

Calculation:

According to the question,

250 = CI - SI

⇒ 250 = [P(1 + R%)T - P] - [\(\frac{(P × R × T)}{100}\)]

⇒ 250 = P{[(1 + R%)T - 1] - [\(\frac{(R × T)}{100}\)]}

⇒ 250 = P{[(1 + 10%)2 - 1] - [\(\frac{(10 × 2)}{100}\)]}

⇒ 250 = P{[(1 + 0.10)2 - 1] - [\(\frac{20}{100}\)]}

⇒ 250 = P{[(1.1)2 - 1] - [0.20]}

⇒ 250 = P{[1.21 - 1] - 0.20}

⇒ 250 = P{0.21 - 0.20}

⇒ 250 = 0.01P

⇒ P = \(\frac{250}{0.01}\) = Rs. 25000

∴ The sum is Rs. 25000.

\({1331 \over 1000}\) Means if 1331 is the amount and 1000 is principal then apply unitery method 

331 is the compound interest for amount 1000 then 

then for pricipal x amount given 1324

questions.question: Rajeev invested Rs. 3,000 for 2 years at compound interest (compounded annually) in a company which paid him interest of Rs. 1,320. What will be the annual rate of interest at which Rajeev invested his money?
questions.questionHtml: Rajeev invested Rs. 3,000 for 2 years at compound interest (compounded annually) in a company which paid him interest of Rs. 1,320. What will be the annual rate of interest at which Rajeev invested his money?
questions.solution:
Given

Principal (P) = Rs. 3000

Compound Interest (CI) = Rs. 1320

Time (t) = 2 years

Concept:

The compound interest formula is CI = P(1 + r/100)t - P, where r is the rate of interest.

Solution:

Substitute the given values in the formula: 1320 = 3000(1 + r/100)^2 - 3000

Solve the equation for r: (1 + r/100)2 = 4320/3000

r: (1 + r/100)2 = 144/100

r = 20%

Hence, the annual rate of interest at which Rajeev invested his money is 20%.

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of money at 10% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 8,100. Compounded annually, what would be the compound interest (in Rs.) on the same sum for the same period at the same rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a sum of money at 10% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 8,100. Compounded annually, what would be the compound interest (in Rs.) on the same sum for the same period at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Effective Simple Interest (SI) rate for 2 years = 10% × 2 = 20%

Effective Compound Interest (CI) rate for 2 years = 10% + 10% + (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 21%

If 20% → Rs. 8,100, then 1% → 8,100 ÷ 20 = 405

⇒ CI (21%) = 405 × 21 = 8,505

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 8,505.

Alternate Method

Given:

Simple Interest (SI) = Rs. 8,100

Rate (R) = 10%

Time (T) = 2 years

Formula Used:

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

CI = P × [(1 + R/100)T − 1]

Calculations:

⇒ P = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T)

⇒ P = (8100 × 100) ÷ (10 × 2)

⇒ P = 810000 ÷ 20 = 40,500

Now, finding the Compound Interest on the Principal calculated:

⇒ CI = 40500 × [(1 + 10/100)2 − 1]

⇒ CI = 40500 × [(11/10)2 − 1]

⇒ CI = 40500 × [121/100 − 1]

⇒ CI = 40500 × (21/100)

⇒ CI = 405 × 21 = 8,505

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 8,505.

Additional Information

Direct Relation between CI and SI for 2 years

When rate (R) and time (T = 2 years) are the same, CI can be directly found using: CI = SI × (1 + R/200).

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference between compound and simple interest on a sum P for 2 years is: Difference = P × (R/100)2.

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

The total effective CI rate for 2 years can be calculated using the successive percentage formula: X + Y + (X × Y)/100.

questions.question: Anil deposited Rs. 8,000 in a two-year fixed deposit scheme on compound interest compounded annually at 5% per annum. Find the maturity value of the fixed deposit.

questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Principal is Rs8,000

Rate = 5%

FORMULA USED:

A = P × ( 1 + R/100)t 

Where, A = Amount, P = Principal , R = Rate of interest t = time in years

CALCULATION:

Here, we have A = Rs8,000, Time = 2 years, Rate = 5% 

⇒ A = P × ( 1 + R/100)t 

⇒ A = 8,000 × ( 1 + 5/100)2  = 8,000 × 21/20 × 21/20 

⇒ A = 8,820.

Hence, the maturity value of fixed deposit is Rs8,820.

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 280900 in 2 years at 6% per annum, interest compounded annually. The sum is:
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 280900 in 2 years at 6% per annum, interest compounded annually. The sum is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rate = 6% = 6/100 = 3/50

Ratio of Principal to Amount for 1 year = 50 : 53

Ratio of Principal to Amount for 2 years = (50)2 : (53)2 = 2500 : 2809

Given Amount = 2809 units = Rs. 280900 ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 100

Principal = 2500 units = 2500 × 100 = Rs. 250000

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 250000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount (A) = Rs. 280900

Time (T) = 2 years

Rate (R) = 6% per annum

Formula Used:

A = P(1 + R/100)T

Calculation:

⇒ 280900 = P(1 + 6/100)2

⇒ 280900 = P(1 + 3/50)2

⇒ 280900 = P(53/50)2

⇒ 280900 = P × (2809 / 2500)

⇒ P = 280900 × (2500 / 2809)

⇒ P = 100 × 2500 = 250000

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 250000.

Additional Information

Compound Interest Formula

When interest is compounded annually, Amount A = P(1 + R/100)T, where P is the principal, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period in years.

Effective Rate of Interest

For 2 years, the effective compound interest rate can be directly calculated using the successive percentage change formula: Reff = R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a sum P at rate R% is given by Diff = P(R/100)2.

questions.question: Find the compound interest (in Rs.) on a sum of Rs. 7,500 for 4 years if the rate of interest is 20% per annum for the first two years and 10% per annum for the next two years. (The interest is compounded annually.)

questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs. 7500

The rate of interest for the first two years = 20%

The rate of interest for the next two years = 10%

Formula used:

CI = P[(1 + R/100)T – 1]

CI = CI1 + CI2

Calculation:

According to the question

CI for the first two year

⇒ CI1 = P[(1 + R/100)T – 1]

⇒ Rs. 7500[(1 + 20/100)2 – 1]

⇒ Rs. 7500[(120/100)2 – 1]

⇒ Rs. 7500[(6/5 × 6/5) – 1]

⇒ Rs. 7500(36/25 – 1)

⇒ Rs. (7500 × 11/25)

⇒ Rs. 3300

Now,

CI for the next two year

P will be = Rs. (7500 + 3300) = Rs. 10800

⇒ CI2 = P[(1 + R/100)T – 1]

⇒ Rs. 10800[(1 + 10/100)2 – 1]

⇒ Rs. 10800[(110/100)2 – 1]

⇒ Rs. 10800[(11/10 × 11/10) – 1]

⇒ Rs. 10800(121/100 – 1)

⇒ Rs. (10800 × 21/100)

⇒ Rs. 2268

Now,

CI = CI1 + CI2

⇒ Rs. (3300 + 2268)

⇒ Rs. 5568

∴ The required CI is Rs. 5,568

questions.question: A bike is purchased for ₹50,000. Its rate depreciates at 10% annually. In how many years will its value be ₹36,450?
questions.questionHtml: A bike is purchased for ₹50,000. Its rate depreciates at 10% annually. In how many years will its value be ₹36,450?
questions.solution:
The value of the bike after T years =\(its \space value \space T\space years\space ago ×(1− \frac{R}{100})^ T\) ⇒  \(36450=50000\times(1+\frac{(-10)}{100})^T\) ⇒  \(729=1000\times(1-\frac{1}{10})^T\)

On comparing both sides, we get T = 3yrs

questions.questionHtml: If a sum becomes Rs. 1,460 in two years and Rs. 1,606 in three years due to the compound interest, then annual rate of interest is∶

Let annual rate of interest be R and principle be P.

Formula∶ Amount = P(1 + R/100)T

⇒ 1460 = P(1 + R/100)2      ----(1)

⇒ 1606 = P(1 + R/100)3      ----(2)

Divide 2 by 1,

⇒ 1606/1460 = (1 + R/100)

⇒ 803/730 – 1 = R/100

⇒ R/100 = (803 – 730)/730 = 73/730 = 1/10

⇒ R = 100/10 = 10%

questions.question: What is the present value of Rs. 9,360 at an interest rate 20% at the end of two years compounded annually?
questions.questionHtml: What is the present value of Rs. 9,360 at an interest rate 20% at the end of two years compounded annually?
questions.solution:
Given:

Amount after 2 years = Rs. 9360

The rate = 20%  . 

Formula used:

Amount ( A ) = Principal ( P ) × (1 + r / 100)n

Calculation:

The present value is 9360 ( after 2 years ). In compound interest,

⇒ A= P × (1 + r / 100)n

⇒ 9360 = P × ( 1 + 20/100)2

⇒ 9360= P × 36/25

⇒ P = 9360 × 25 / 36 = 6500 

∴ The  present value of Rs. 9,360 at an interest rate 20% at the end of two years compounded annually is 6500.

questions.question: At what percentage rate, compound interest compounded annually for a sum of Rs. 40,000, will amount to Rs. 44,100 in two years?
questions.questionHtml: At what percentage rate, compound interest compounded annually for a sum of Rs. 40,000, will amount to Rs. 44,100 in two years?
questions.solution:
Given:

P = 40,000 and A = 44,100 and t = 2 years

Calculation:

A = P (1 + r/100)t

⇒ 44,100 = 40,000 (1 + r/100)2

⇒ (1 + r/100)2 = 44,100/40,000

⇒ (1 + r/100) = √44,100/40,000

⇒ r/100 = 21/20 - 1

⇒ r/100 = 1/20

⇒ r = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%

Shortcut Trick

Rs. 40,000, will amount to Rs. 44,100 in two years

So, Principal : Amount

⇒ √ 40000 : √ 44100

⇒ 20 : 21

So, the rate of interest is [(21 - 20)/20] × 100 = 5%

questions.question: The compound interest on ₹ 4,000 after 3 year is ₹ 630.50. Then the rate of interest compounded yearly is:

Calculation:

⇒ 630.50 = 4000[(1 + rate/100)3 – 1]

⇒ 630.50/4000 = [(1 + rate/100)3 – 1]

⇒ (1261/8000) + 1 = [(1 + rate/100)3]

⇒ 9261/8000 = [(1 + rate/100)3]

⇒ 21/20 = [(1 + rate/100)]

questions.question: If the difference between the compound interest and simple interest at 17% on a sum of money for 2 years (compounded annually) is Rs. 433.50, then the sum (in Rs.) is:
questions.questionHtml: If the difference between the compound interest and simple interest at 17% on a sum of money for 2 years (compounded annually) is Rs. 433.50, then the sum (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Rate of interest = 17%

Time = 2 years

The difference between CI and SI = Rs. 433.50

Formula used:

Simple interest = P × R% × T

Calculation:

Let the principal be Rs. x.

SI = P × R% × T

⇒ SI = x × 17% × 2

⇒ SI = x × 17/100 × 2

⇒ SI = 34x/100

⇒ SI = 0.34x

In the case of CI:

1st year CI = P × R% × T

⇒ 1st year CI = x × 17% × 1

⇒ 1st year CI = 17x/100

⇒ 1st year CI = 0.17x

Amount after 1st year = P + CI 

⇒ Amount = x + 0.17x

⇒ Amount = 1.17x

2nd year CI = 1.17x × 17% × 1

⇒ 2nd year CI = 0.1989x

Total CI = 1st year CI + 2nd year CI

⇒ CI = 0.17x + 0.1989x

⇒ CI = 0.3689x

Required difference = CI – SI

⇒ 433.50 = 0.3689x – 0.34x

⇒ 433.50 = 0.0289x

⇒ x = 433.50/0.0289

⇒ x = Rs. 15000

∴ The sum is Rs. 15000.

questions.question: The compound interest and the amount obtained, on a certain sum of money are ₨. 820 and ₨. 8,820 respectively after 2 years. If the rate of interest compounded yearly, then the rate of interest is:
questions.questionHtml: The compound interest and the amount obtained, on a certain sum of money are ₨. 820 and ₨. 8,820 respectively after 2 years. If the rate of interest compounded yearly, then the rate of interest is:
questions.solution:
Formula:

A = P (1 + r/100)t 

Calculation:

Amount = Rs. 8820 

CI = Rs. 820

Principal = Rs. 8820 - Rs. 820 = Rs. 8000

According to the formula

8820 = 8000 (1 + r/100)2

⇒ (1 + r/100)2 = 8820/8000

⇒ (1 + r/100)2 = 441/400

⇒ (1 + r/100) = √441/400

⇒ (1 + r/100) = 21/20

⇒ r/100 = 21/20 - 1

⇒ r/100 = 1/20

⇒ r = 5%

∴ The rate of interest is 5%.

questions.question: If a sum on compound interest (compounded yearly) becomes three times in 4 years, then with the same interest rate, the sum will become 81 times in:
questions.questionHtml: If a sum on compound interest (compounded yearly) becomes three times in 4 years, then with the same interest rate, the sum will become 81 times in:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If a sum becomes x times in T years, it becomes xn times in n × T years.

Given: Sum becomes 31 times in 4 years (x = 3, T = 4).

To find: Time to become 81 times.

Since 81 = 34, here n = 4.

Required time = n × T = 4 × 4 = 16 years.

∴ The correct answer is 16 years.

Alternate Method

Given: Sum becomes 3 times in 4 years at Compound Interest.

Formula Used: A = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ Case 1: 3P = P(1 + r/100)4

⇒ 3 = (1 + r/100)4 — (Equation 1)

⇒ Case 2: 81P = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 81 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (3)4 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ [(1 + r/100)4]4 = (1 + r/100)t [From Eq. 1]

⇒ (1 + r/100)16 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ t = 16 years

∴ The correct answer is 16 years.

Additional Information

Compound Interest Formula

The amount A on a principal P for t years at rate r% compounded annually is A = P(1 + r/100)t.

Successive Growth in CI

In compound interest, the amount grows geometrically. If a sum doubles in T years, it becomes 22 times in 2T years, 23 times in 3T years, and so on.

Rule of 72

A quick shortcut to estimate the time required to double an investment is T ≈ 72 ÷ r, where r is the annual interest rate.

questions.question: If the compound interest @ 10% p.a. compounded half-yearly for \(1\frac{1}{2}\) year is Rs. 2,522, principle amount is∶
questions.questionHtml: If the compound interest @ 10% p.a. compounded half-yearly for \(1\frac{1}{2}\) year is Rs. 2,522, principle amount is∶
questions.solution:
Let the principle be P.

Amount = Rs. 2522

Rate of interest = 10%, Time = 3/2 year

Since the interest is compounded half-yearly.

∴ Actual rate of interest = R = 10/2 = 5%

And the number of terms = N = 3/2 × 2 = 3

Formula for compound interest,

Compound Interest = P (1 + R/100)N – P

2522 = P (1.053 – 1)

∴ P = 2522/0.157625 = Rs. 16000

Alternate Solution∶

R = 5% = 1/20, n = 3 years

∴ P = 8000, Given that CI = 2522

Compound Interest = 400 × 3 + 20 × 3 + 1 = 1261

∵ 1261 → 2522
